questions.q: What three real fixes does the northfield-orders-etl PySpark script apply to the raw order data?
options: Converts order_date to a real date type, normalizes region casing, and computes an order_total column
Converts the data to JSON format
Deletes all rows with missing values and stops there
Renames every column to generic names like col1, col2
questions.explain: The job types order_date, normalizes/trims region, adds a computed order_total, and dedupes by order_id.

questions.q: Where does northfield-orders-etl write its output, and in what format?
options: s3://northfield-curated-zone/orders/, as uncompressed CSV
Back into northfield-raw-zone, overwriting the source CSVs
Directly into a Redshift table, no S3 output
s3://northfield-curated-zone/orders/, as partitioned Parquet with Snappy compression
questions.explain: The job writes partitioned Parquet (Snappy-compressed) into the curated zone bucket, partitioned by the same dt key as the raw zone.

questions.q: What would happen to northfield-orders-etl's runtime and cost if job bookmarks were disabled, once the raw zone has a year of daily partitions?
options: Nothing would change — bookmarks have no effect on runtime
The job would fail to start without bookmarks
It would process data faster without bookmarks
Every run would reprocess the entire raw zone history instead of just the new day's partition, inflating runtime and DPU cost
questions.explain: Job bookmarks track already-processed data so incremental runs only touch new partitions; without them, every run reprocesses everything.

questions.q: Why does the curated output get partitioned by dt, the same key as the raw zone?
options: Because Parquet files cannot be written without partitioning
To make the file names easier to read
It's required by the Glue Data Catalog for all tables
So Athena and Redshift Spectrum can prune partitions on the curated side too, not just the raw side
questions.explain: Matching the partition key end-to-end lets query engines skip irrelevant partitions on both the raw and curated data.

questions.q: Why is Parquet preferred over the raw zone's CSV for the curated output?
options: Parquet files can't be partitioned, which simplifies the pipeline
It's a compressed, columnar format, so queries reading only a few columns don't have to scan whole rows
Parquet is required for any S3 bucket used by Redshift
CSV cannot be read by Athena at all
questions.explain: Parquet's columnar, compressed layout is cheaper to query and store than row-based CSV — exactly why the ETL job converts to it.
